questions.question: Nandan had some marbles. When he distributed the marbles equally among 32 children, he found that 4 marbles were left. Had he distributed the marbles equally among 41 children and 48 children, he still would have had 13 and 20 marbles, respectively, left with him. But when he distributed them equally among 53 children, no marble was left. The number of marbles that Nandan initially had may lie between __________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Check the common difference between **divisors** and **remainders**.

32 − 4 = 28, 41 − 13 = 28, 48 − 20 = 28.

Number = LCM(32, 41, 48) × k − 28, and it must be divisible by 53.

LCM(32, 41, 48) = 7872. For k = 1, Number = 7872 − 28 = 7844.

7844 ÷ 53 = 148 (Remainder 0). So, 7844 is the number.

**∴ The correct answer is 7834 and 7854.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8aae85ef718862e22a50564a627c80d4869327bb1ec4d8991b806deb4aa5cf6f.png] 
**Given:** Divisors (d₁, d₂, d₃) = 32, 41, 48 | Remainders (r₁, r₂, r₃) = 4, 13, 20.

⇒ Common difference (d − r) = 32 − 4 = 28; 41 − 13 = 28; 48 − 20 = 28.

⇒ LCM(32, 41, 48) = 2⁵ × 41 × 3 = 32 × 123 = 7872.

⇒ General form: N = 7872k − 28.

⇒ Condition: N must be exactly divisible by 53.

⇒ Test k = 1: N = 7872(1) − 28 = 7844.

⇒ Verification: 7844 = 53 × 148 + 0. (Condition satisfied).

⇒ 7844 lies between 7834 and 7854.

**∴ The correct answer is 7834 and 7854.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM with Common Difference

When (Divisor − Remainder) is constant (say x), the number is LCM(Divisors) × k − x.

LCM with Same Remainder

If every divisor leaves the same remainder r, the number is LCM(Divisors) × k + r.

Divisibility Rule of 53

To check if a number is divisible by 53, add 16 times the last digit to the rest of the number.</p

questions.question: If 674 bananas were distributed among three monkeys in the ratio (17)/(2) : (14)/(6) : (2)/(5) respectively, how many bananas did the third monkey get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify ratio: 17/2 : 14/6 : 2/5 → 17/2 : 7/3 : 2/5.

LCM of denominators (2, 3, 5) = 30.

New Ratio: (17/2 × 30) : (7/3 × 30) : (2/5 × 30) = 255 : 70 : 12.

Total parts = 255 + 70 + 12 = 337 units.

337 units = 674 ⇒ 1 unit = 2 bananas.

Third monkey (12 units) = 12 × 2 = 24 bananas.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30ed018d4cc23ca3c667bd3069713aee376da66a56521e6008fcc3ecf63bbd8a.png] 

**Given:**

Total bananas = 674

Ratio = 17/2 : 14/6 : 2/5

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, simplify the fraction ratio by multiplying with the **LCM** of denominators 2, 6, and 5.

⇒ LCM(2, 6, 5) = 30.

⇒ Monkey 1 = (17/2) × 30 = 255

⇒ Monkey 2 = (14/6) × 30 = 70

⇒ Monkey 3 = (2/5) × 30 = 12

⇒ Total Ratio Sum = 255 + 70 + 12 = 337

⇒ Share of third monkey = (12 ÷ 337) × 674

⇒ Share = 12 × 2 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Simplification

To convert a fractional ratio a/b : c/d into a whole number ratio, multiply each term by the **LCM** of the denominators b and d.

Proportional Division

If a total quantity X is divided in the ratio a : b : c, then the share of the third part is calculated as [c ÷ (a + b + c)] × X.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of (a : b) and (c : d) is found by multiplying corresponding terms, resulting in (ac : bd).</p

questions.question: The mode of the observations 24, 33, 32, 24, 28, 24, 29, 25, 25, 34, 27, 26, 22, 34, 27, 24 and 30 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Mode** is defined as the observation that appears **most frequently** in a data set.

By scanning the data: **24** appears 4 times, while 25, 27, and 34 appear only 2 times each.

All other numbers (22, 26, 28, 29, 30, 32, 33) appear only once.

Since **24** has the **maximum frequency**, it is the mode of the given observations.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations = 24, 33, 32, 24, 28, 24, 29, 25, 25, 34, 27, 26, 22, 34, 27, 24, 30

**Formula:** Mode = Value with the highest frequency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b26e0d324b86ffdaea8560c2e49832924bbc15ca653f35677f25771f76e50e6.png] 

To find the mode, we construct a **frequency table** for the given data:

⇒ Frequency of 22 = 1

⇒ **Frequency of 24 = 4**

⇒ Frequency of 25 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 26 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 27 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 28 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 29 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 30 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 32 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 33 = 1

⇒ Frequency of 34 = 2

⇒ Comparing all frequencies, the **maximum frequency** is 4.

⇒ The observation corresponding to the maximum frequency is 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Types of Data Sets

A data set with one mode is **unimodal**. If it has two modes, it is **bimodal**, and if it has more than two, it is **multimodal**.

Median Calculation

To find the **Median**, arrange data in ascending order. If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)/2)th term. If n is even, Median = Average of (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms.</p

questions.question: If the length of a cuboid is 33 cm, breadth is 4 cm and volume is 7524 cm³, then find the height (in cm) of the cuboid.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Height** = **Volume** ÷ (**Length** × **Breadth**)

Height = 7524 ÷ (33 × 4)

Height = 7524 ÷ 132 = 57 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 57 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length (l)** = 33 cm

**Breadth (b)** = 4 cm

**Volume (V)** = 7524 cm³

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of a cuboid** = **l** × **b** × **h**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa2c67171c110746b8b010dd34f060596d7cc45350895cc51a395b910c81d3a9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 7524 = 33 × 4 × **h**

⇒ 7524 = 132 × **h**

⇒ **h** = 7524 ÷ 132

⇒ **h** = 57 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 57 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area is calculated as 2 × (lb + bh + hl).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can fit in a cuboid is given by √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area

Area of four walls = 2 × **height** × (**length** + **breadth**).</p

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of the equation x² − x − 6 = 0, find the value of α⁴ + β⁴.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the **quadratic equation** x² − x − 6 = 0 into (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0.

The **roots** are α = 3 and β = −2.

Now, substitute these **roots** directly into the required expression α⁴ + β⁴.

α⁴ + β⁴ = (3)⁴ + (−2)⁴ = 81 + 16 = 97.

**∴ The correct answer is 97.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² − x − 6 = 0

For a **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, the coefficients are a = 1, b = −1, and c = −6.

**Formula Used:** **Sum of roots** (α + β) = −b/a and **Product of roots** (αβ) = c/a.

⇒ α + β = −(−1)/1 = 1

⇒ αβ = −6/1 = −6

To find α⁴ + β⁴, first find **α² + β²**:

⇒ α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ

⇒ α² + β² = (1)² − 2(−6) = 1 + 12 = 13

Now, square the above result to find **α⁴ + β⁴**:

⇒ α⁴ + β⁴ = (α² + β²)² − 2(αβ)²

⇒ α⁴ + β⁴ = (13)² − 2(−6)²

⇒ α⁴ + β⁴ = 169 − 2(36) = 169 − 72 = 97

**∴ The correct answer is 97.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Roots and Coefficients

For the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **sum of roots** is −b/a and the **product of roots** is c/a. This allows solving symmetric expressions without finding individual roots.

Algebraic Identities for Powers

Useful identities include α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ and α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β).

Nature of Roots

The **discriminant** (D = b² − 4ac) determines if roots are real and distinct (D > 0), real and equal (D = 0), or non-real complex (D < 0).</p

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 27 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 28 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be one-fourth filled, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let filling pipe be **A** and emptying pipe be **B**.

Net efficiency for filling full tank = (1/27 − 1/28) = 1/(27 × 28) per hour.

Time to fill full tank = 27 × 28 = 756 hours.

Time to fill 1/4th tank = 756 ÷ 4 = 189 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 189 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Pipe A (Inlet)**

 **Pipe B (Outlet)**

⇒ **Total Capacity** of tank = LCM of 27 and 28 = 756 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 756 ÷ 27 = +28 units/hr.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 756 ÷ 28 = −27 units/hr.

⇒ Combined efficiency (A + B) = 28 − 27 = 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Work to be done = 1/4 of total capacity = 756 ÷ 4 = 189 units.

⇒ Required Time = 189 ÷ 1 = 189 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 189 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipe efficiency is taken as **positive (+)** and outlet (emptying) pipe efficiency is taken as **negative (−)**.

Net Time Formula

If an inlet fills in 'x' hours and outlet empties in 'y' hours, net time to fill is **(xy) ÷ (y − x)**, provided y > x.</p

questions.question: In covering a distance of 90 km, Anirudh takes 3 hours more than Burhan. If Anirudh doubles his speed, then he would take 2 hours less than Burhan. Anirudh's initial speed is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Speed ratio** of **Anirudh** = 1 : 2

**Time ratio** of **Anirudh** (inverse of speed) = 2 : 1

Difference in time units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit

Actual time difference = 3 hours (more) + 2 hours (less) = 5 hours

∴ 1 unit = 5 hours → Initial time (2 units) = 10 hours

Initial Speed = Distance ÷ Initial Time = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5867ab45e357ccc0d0afd57cb0a195d413be50753b144c9e2cf4c8af46c81a84.png] 

**Given:** Total **distance** = 90 km. Let **Anirudh's** speed be x km/hr and **Burhan's** time be TB.

**Formula:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Case 1: 90/x = TB + 3

⇒ Case 2: 90/(2x) = TB − 2

⇒ Subtracting Case 2 from Case 1:

⇒ (90/x) − (90/2x) = (TB + 3) − (TB − 2)

⇒ 90/2x = 5

⇒ 45/x = 5

⇒ x = 45/5 = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Inversity

When **distance** is constant, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time**. If speed ratio is a:b, then time ratio is b:a.

Average Speed

For a constant distance traveled at two different speeds x and y, **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is the sum (s₁ + s₂); if in the **same direction**, it is the difference (s₁ − s₂).</p

questions.question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 28 g/cm³. Its internal and external radii are 2 cm and 5 cm, respectively. What is the approximate weight (in kg) of the shell?

(Take pi = (22)/(7), Density = (Mass)/(Volume)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Mass** = **Density** × **Volume**

**Volume** of shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × (5³ − 2³) = (4/3) × (22/7) × 117 cm³

**Mass** = 28 × (4/3) × (22/7) × 117 = 4 × 4 × 22 × 39 = 13728 g

**Mass in kg** = 13728 ÷ 1000 = 13.728 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 13.728 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Internal radius (r)** = 2 cm

**External radius (R)** = 5 cm

**Density** = 28 g/cm³

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of hollow shell** = (4/3)π(R³ − r³)

**Mass** = **Volume** × **Density**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b4366c7f16788eb96595027fd24a82b17687dba197648dbba7af277fca7e953.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Volume** = (4/3) × (22/7) × (5³ − 2³)

⇒ **Volume** = (4/3) × (22/7) × (125 − 8)

⇒ **Volume** = (4/3) × (22/7) × 117 = 490.28 cm³

⇒ **Mass (in grams)** = 490.28 × 28

⇒ **Mass** = 13728 g

⇒ **Mass (in kg)** = 13728 ÷ 1000 = 13.728 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 13.728 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Volume of Solid Sphere**

The volume of a **solid sphere** is given by V = (4/3)πr³.

**Surface Area of Sphere**

The **total surface area** of a sphere is 4πr².

**Density Conversion**

To convert **g/cm³** to **kg/m³**, multiply by 1000. Here, weight is asked in kg, so we divide total grams by 1000.</p

questions.question: Kalpana and Sudha got 624 and 720 marks, respectively, in the same examination. If Kalpana scored 26% marks, then what is the percentage of marks scored by Sudha?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Percentage of Sudha** = (**Sudha's marks** ÷ **Kalpana's marks**) × **Kalpana's %**

⇒ **Percentage** = (720 ÷ 624) × 26%

⇒ **Percentage** = (15 ÷ 13) × 26% = 15 × 2% = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks obtained by **Kalpana** = 624

Percentage obtained by **Kalpana** = 26%

Marks obtained by **Sudha** = 720

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7d4c372e319a2051dc261469fc1e991d245f5d8505b7203a2481d41cfd7d774.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the **Total Marks** of the examination be **x**.

⇒ According to the question, 26% of **x** = 624

⇒ (26 ÷ 100) × **x** = 624

⇒ **x** = (624 × 100) ÷ 26

⇒ **x** = 24 × 100 = 2400

⇒ **Percentage of Sudha** = (**Marks obtained** ÷ **Total marks**) × 100

⇒ **Percentage** = (720 ÷ 2400) × 100

⇒ **Percentage** = 720 ÷ 24 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

To find the percentage increase or decrease: **Change %** = (**Difference** ÷ **Original Value**) × 100.

Base Change Property

If person A scores x% marks and person B scores y% marks, the **ratio of their marks** is equal to the **ratio of their percentages**.

Pass Marks Calculation

If a student fails by 'a' marks or passes by 'b' marks, **Total Marks** = (**Difference in marks** ÷ **Difference in %**) × 100.</p

questions.question: The population of a village was 1,20,000. It increased by 10% in the first year and increased by 30% in the second year. Its population after two years is _______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **successive percentage increase** formula for two years.

Net Percentage Increase = a + b + (a × b)/100 = 10 + 30 + (10 × 30)/100 = 43%.

Final Population = 120000 × 1.43 = 1,71,600.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,71,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial population = 1,20,000; Increase in 1st year = 10%; Increase in 2ⁿd year = 30%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d696a1389270a871c623549314478ae842cd531d94650cf3d404087be1ed4ac.png] 

**Formula:** Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

⇒ Population after 1st year = 1,20,000 + 10% of 1,20,000

⇒ Population after 1st year = 1,20,000 + 12,000 = 1,32,000

⇒ Population after 2ⁿd year = 1,32,000 + 30% of 1,32,000

⇒ Population after 2ⁿd year = 1,32,000 + 39,600

⇒ Population after 2ⁿd year = 1,71,600

**∴ The correct answer is 1,71,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value changes by a% then b%, the net change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of x% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 + x/100). For 10%, multiply by 1.1; for 30%, multiply by 1.3.

Population Decrease

If the population decreases, use a negative sign in the formula: Final = Initial × (1 − r/100)ⁿ.</p

questions.question: The percentage profit earned by selling a table lamp for ₹863 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same table lamp for ₹433. At what price (in ₹) should the table lamp be sold to make 25% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Profit% = Loss%** for two selling prices, **CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2**.

CP = (863 + 433) ÷ 2 = 1296 ÷ 2 = ₹648.

To gain **25% profit**, required SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

Required SP = 648 × 125 ÷ 100 = 648 × 5 ÷ 4.

Required SP = 162 × 5 = ₹810.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹810.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹863 (Profit), SP₂ = ₹433 (Loss), Profit% = Loss%.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc1d8d483e71471d3f74e7659268785ccce9a9d94311016327c84e449586476d.png] 

⇒ Since Profit% = Loss% and both are on the same CP, the absolute Profit = absolute Loss.

⇒ (863 − CP) = (CP − 433)

⇒ 2 × CP = 863 + 433 = 1296

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 1296 ÷ 2 = ₹648

⇒ Desired Profit = 25% of 648 = 648 ÷ 4 = ₹162

⇒ **New Selling Price** = CP + Profit = 648 + 162 = ₹810

**∴ The correct answer is ₹810.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equating Profit and Loss

If numerical profit equals numerical loss, the Cost Price is always the **arithmetic mean** of the two Selling Prices.

Percentage Calculations

To find 25% of a value, it is often faster to **divide the value by 4**. Adding this result to the original CP gives the SP for a 25% profit.

questions.question: The sum of nine times the present age of A and eight times the present age of B is 148 years. Two times the present age of B exceeds two times the present age of A by 20 years. What will be the sum of the ages (in years) of A and B, 6 years from now?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given 2B − 2A = 20 ⇒ **B − A = 10**.

Substitute B = A + 10 in 9A + 8B = 148: 9A + 8(A + 10) = 148 ⇒ 17A = 68 ⇒ **A = 4**.

Then **B = 14**. Sum of present ages = 18 years.

Sum after 6 years = 18 + 2 × 6 = 30 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/363816f42dbe1b795679ff794eff4820ec72eff902471dee44a12650baa72a89.png] 

**Given:**

Let the present age of **A** be **x** and **B** be **y**.

⇒ 9x + 8y = 148 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 2y − 2x = 20 ⇒ y − x = 10 ⇒ y = x + 10 --- (Equation 2)

**Calculations:**

questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 4 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 9 (1)/(3) hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?

questions.question:
In the given figure, AB and CD are two parallel lines and PQ is a transversal line . Find the measure of ∠PMB.

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **AB || CD** and **PQ** is a **transversal line**, the angle ∠MND and the given angle ∠DNQ form a **linear pair** on the straight line PQ.

⇒ ∠MND = 180° − 50° = 130°

Since **corresponding angles** are equal for parallel lines, we have:

⇒ ∠PMB = ∠MND = 130°

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **AB || CD** (parallel lines)

⇒ **PQ** is a **transversal line** intersecting AB at M and CD at N.

⇒ ∠DNQ = 50°

**Properties Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Angles on a straight line sum up to 180°.

2. **Corresponding Angles Postulate:** When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03039929e88d8d00e36c8b0bd756998dc01025dc3e2d250b1788be10a8f616d7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠MND + ∠DNQ = 180° (Linear pair on transversal line PQ)

⇒ ∠MND + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠MND = 180° − 50° = 130°

Since AB || CD and PQ is the transversal line:

⇒ ∠PMB = ∠MND (Corresponding angles)

⇒ ∠PMB = 130°

**Option Analysis:**

⇒ **Option (1) 120°** is incorrect because the supplementary angle to 50° is 130°, not 120°.

⇒ **Option (3) 100°** is incorrect because the angle is determined by the linear pair relation with 50°, which yields 130°.

⇒ **Option (4) 50°** is incorrect because ∠PMB is an obtuse angle, whereas 50° is an acute angle (∠BMN = 50°).

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the angles in matching corners are called corresponding angles and they are equal.

Alternate Exterior Angles

Alternate exterior angles are equal when lines are parallel. For example, ∠PMA and ∠DNQ are alternate exterior angles.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Consecutive interior angles lie on the same side of the transversal and inside the parallel lines. Their sum is always 180°.</p

⇒ Average Speed = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Harmonic Mean for Equal Distances

If a car covers two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |v₁ − v₂|. In opposite directions, it is (v₁ + v₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: If x² + (1)/(x²) = 83, x > 0, then find the value of x³ - (1)/(x³).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If x² + 1/x² = n, then (x − 1/x) = √(n − 2).

Here n = 83 → x − 1/x = √(83 − 2) = 9.

Shortcut for **x³ − 1/x³** = k³ + 3k, where k = (x − 1/x).

Required value = 9³ + 3(9) = 729 + 27 = 756.

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x² + 1/x² = 83

x > 0

**Formula Used:**

1. **Algebraic identity**: (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

2. **Algebraic identity**: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² − 2×x×(1/x)

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 83 − 2

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 81

⇒ x − 1/x = √81 = 9

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)(x² + 1/x² + (x×1/x))

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 9 × (83 + 1)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 9 × 84 = 756

**∴ The correct answer is 756.**

**__Additional Information__**

Positive Power Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Negative Power Relation

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2 and x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Relationship between (x+1/x) and (x-1/x)

(x + 1/x)² − (x − 1/x)² = 4.</p

questions.question: Find the value of 7secA(1 + sin A) (sec A − tanA) − 4
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put **A = 0°** as the expression is valid for all values of A.

sin 0° = 0, cos 0° = 1, sec 0° = 1, tan 0° = 0.

⇒ 7 × sec 0° (1 + sin 0°) (sec 0° − tan 0°) − 4

⇒ 7 × 1 (1 + 0) (1 − 0) − 4 = 7 × 1 × 1 × 1 − 4 = 7 − 4 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 7sec A (1 + sin A) (sec A − tan A) − 4

**Formula Used:** sec A = 1/cos A, tan A = sin A/cos A, (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², 1 − sin²A = cos²A

⇒ 7sec A (1 + sin A) (1/cos A − sin A/cos A) − 4

⇒ 7sec A (1 + sin A) [(1 − sin A) / cos A] − 4

⇒ 7sec A [(1 + sin A)(1 − sin A) / cos A] − 4

⇒ 7sec A [(1 − sin²A) / cos A] − 4

⇒ 7(1/cos A) [cos²A / cos A] − 4

⇒ 7(1/cos A) × cos A − 4

⇒ 7 − 4 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

sin²A + cos²A = 1, sec²A − tan²A = 1, and cosec²A − cot²A = 1.

Value Substitution Method

In trigonometric expressions with no conditions, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, 45° often yields the result quickly.</p

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 11, then x² + 1/x² is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an **algebraic expression** of the form **x + 1/x = k**, the value of **x² + 1/x²** is given by the formula **k² − 2**.

Given: **x + 1/x = 11**, so **k = 11**.

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 11² − 2**

⇒ **121 − 2 = 119**

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **x + 1/x = 11**

To find the value of **x² + 1/x²**, we use the **square identity**:

Formula: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

⇒ **(x + 1/x)² = (11)²**

⇒ **x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x) = 121**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² + 2 = 121**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 121 − 2**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 119**

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Sign Identity

If **x − 1/x = k**, then **x² + 1/x² = k² + 2**.

Cubic Identity

If **x + 1/x = k**, then **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Higher Power (Fourth)

To find **x⁴ + 1/x⁴**, square the value of **(x² + 1/x²)** and subtract 2.</p

 2 dfrac{2}{9} times 2 dfrac{2}{3} times 567 + 8 dfrac{3}{4}
In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle measures 124°. What is the measure of each of the base angles?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle**, base angles are equal.

Sum of base angles = 180° − **Vertex angle**

Sum = 180° − 124° = 56°

Each base angle = 56° ÷ 2 = 28°

**∴ The correct answer is 28° and 28°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Vertex angle** (top angle) = 124°

Triangle type = **Isosceles Triangle**

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles of a triangle = 180°

In an **isosceles triangle**, angles opposite to equal sides are equal (Base angles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d77a218bbbbe5327f92a336a9b2f66c653339f26052b1675f7e93d3a434bce8b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let each **base angle** be x.

⇒ 124° + x + x = 180°

⇒ 124° + 2x = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 124°

⇒ 2x = 56°

⇒ x = 56° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 28°

**∴ The correct answer is 28° and 28°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Properties

A triangle with at least two equal sides. The angles opposite to these sides are always equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Equilateral Triangle

A special case of an isosceles triangle where all three sides and all three angles (each 60°) are equal.</p
